standards.mechanism: Subnet placement by aws_subnet.availability_zone from the aws_availability_zones data source
Mocked-provider plan assertion (mock_provider, mock_data defaults, run with command = plan)

assumptions: Terraform 1.15.3 ran locally; CI pins 1.17.1. infra/terraform/README.md and required_version (~> 1.11) accept both.
The test asserts the literal "eu-west-1b", the second name of the mocked zone list, so it checks the outcome rather than repeating the index expression.
The locals comment said the first zone was the instance's; it now says the instance's subnet is in the second. No other line changed besides the index and the new comment on aws_subnet.public.
infra/terraform/README.md names no zone for the instance, so it is unchanged.

On the next apply, changing availability_zone replaces aws_subnet.public (the argument forces a new resource), and with it the instance (subnet_id forces a new resource) and the route-table association; the Elastic IP is kept and re-associated. Anything on the instance's root volume is lost. Not planned against real state here (no aws calls), so the exact plan is unverified: run terraform plan in envs/dev before apply and read the replacements.

c7i-flex.large in the second zone is confirmed only for af-south-1 (from the brief). For the other four allowed regions (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-central-1) it is unverified; zone names also map to different physical zones per account.
